content:
General Motors first announced back in 2023 that it would drop CarPlay from all its future EVs, and later came up with a series of absurd excuses—at one point even implying the decision was one Steve Jobs himself would have endorsed.

But it seems there's now an exception. Since the policy shift at the time was reportedly based on customer feedback, perhaps GM is now starting to reconsider its major decision...

The news was spotted by Engadget from a CarBuzz report.

Cadillac's online configurator has opened up for several 2027 models, and we noticed that the Lyriq still comes standard with CarPlay and Android Auto. The Lyriq is Cadillac's first all-electric vehicle and a tech-heavy model that we think is steadily becoming one of the best luxury EVs on the market. A Cadillac representative told CarBuzz: "Cadillac continues to refine its infotainment strategy for its EV lineup based on customer feedback, while also prioritizing the native in-vehicle experience."

Further reading: We found customers won't actually buy a luxury EV without CarPlay.

Engadget also noted a handy workaround for owners of other GM vehicles that don't support CarPlay.

Does this mean GM's plan to wean everyone off CarPlay is coming to an end? Share your thoughts in the comments.
